name: University of Lincoln

settingEvidence.evidence: explore our modern, city centre campus

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students on full-time courses starting in 2027/28 (Lincoln's 'Fees Group D', which all three courses here link to). Lincoln says the UK fee may increase year on year in line with government policy. An optional placement year costs £2,010 and a full study-abroad year £1,505 (2027/28).

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £129–£191 a week depending on the residence: 179 High Street £129–£179, Valentine Court £149–£159, The Gateway £159–£179, St Marks £175–£191, Cygnet Wharf £191. Contracts run 40 to 51 weeks. Lincoln's page doesn't say which year these prices are for or what is included.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days (listed under 'Open Days 2026'): 7 November 2026 and 5 December 2026, both 9am-3pm on campus. No later dates are listed yet.

source.evidence: 07 Nov Undergraduate Open Day 9am-3pm 05 Dec Undergraduate Open Day 9am-3pm

contextual.summary: Lincoln automatically considers Home (UK) fee applicants who meet its criteria for a contextual offer one grade lower than the standard offer (for example 104 instead of 112 UCAS Tariff points, BCC instead of BBC).
contextual.typicalReduction: One grade (8 UCAS Tariff points) lower than the standard entry requirements for most undergraduate courses, from a minimum of two full A levels or equivalent (e.g. 112 points / BBC becomes 104 points / BCC).

criteria.detail: You live in an area with a high level of deprivation or a low number of people going to university (usually decided by your postcode), or you live in a Lincolnshire local authority area.

Your school or college's academic performance is lower than the national average, or a small number of its pupils go on to higher education. Schools in Lincoln's Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) partnership get the same reduction in tariff.
You receive, or have received, free school meals (the UCAS application asks you to confirm this).
You are a care leaver (tick the 'in care' box on the UCAS application form).
You have a disability, including long-term health conditions.

contextual.rulesText: If you meet Lincoln's general criteria for a contextual offer you are asked to achieve one grade lower than the standard entry requirements for most undergraduate courses, from a minimum of two full A levels or equivalent. You don't need to do anything extra: apply through UCAS and you are automatically considered. You must be a Home (UK) fee payer; contextual offers only apply to full-time undergraduate courses (foundation programmes are excluded). Any subject-specific requirements must still be met. The criteria listed are Lincoln's '2026 Entry' wording.

source.evidence: If you meet our general criteria for a contextual offer, we will ask you to achieve one grade lower than the standard entry requirements for the majority of our undergraduate degree courses.

notes: Lincoln publishes entry requirements as UCAS Tariff points from at least two A levels (Economics and Accountancy and Finance 104 to 112 points; Business and Management 96 to 104 points), with BBC (or BCC for Business and Management) given as the A level equivalent of the top of the range. Its offer guide says other grade mixes such as ABC can reach 112 points, and an EPQ can be counted once two A levels are achieved.
No admissions test: Lincoln is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry and no course page names a test.

Lincoln's Accountancy, Finance and Economics subject page lists only two undergraduate degrees (Accountancy and Finance; Economics). No Business Economics, Economics and Finance, Economics with Politics or PPE degree was found.

Lincoln's outreach pages describe workshops and visits booked by schools and colleges (including a 'Making the most of post-16' workshop for Year 12) and Year 10 'Prepare for Your Future' events; no Year 12 summer school or access programme relevant to Economics was found, so no programmes are recorded.
